findings.summary: The Save affordance now requires a nonblank birthday, which contradicts the birthday being optional everywhere else and would block saving contacts without one.
findings.evidence: preconditions: [Owner session, Nonblank name, Nonblank birthday] vs. BirthdayField 'Optional birthday as month and day' and criterion 'an optional month-day birthday'

findings.summary: The stored birthday type is a full local-date, but the UI lets the user leave the year blank, so a month-day birthday cannot be represented.
findings.evidence: { name: birthday, type: local-date, optional: true } vs. 'Optional birthday as month and day; the year may be left blank'

findings.summary: The birthday field has cardinality 'exactly one' despite being optional, and neither operation.contact.save nor the journey's branch conditions cover the birthday validation the criterion now claims.
findings.evidence: cardinality: exactly one; operation.contact.save preconditions: [Owner session, Nonblank name]; s4 branches only 'save, name nonblank' / 'save, name blank'
